questions.question: A system uses fixed handwritten rules with no learning component. Why does it fall outside the CT-AI scope of AI-based systems?

options.A: It lacks a learning or adaptive component, so ML-specific test concerns such as training data and model drift do not apply
options.C: Testing rules requires no test design
options.D: AI scope covers every software system

questions.explanation: The syllabus targets systems whose behaviour is learned from data; purely rule-based logic is tested with conventional techniques.

questions.question: Why does the distinction between narrow AI and general AI matter when scoping test effort?

options.A: Narrow AI has a bounded task context that makes requirements and oracles definable, unlike general intelligence
options.B: General AI is already widely deployed
options.D: The distinction has no practical effect

questions.explanation: Testability depends on a definable task and expected behaviour, which only narrow, task-specific AI provides.

questions.question: A vendor claims their product uses AI because it contains a linear regression. What should the tester establish first?

options.A: Whether a learned model actually influences behaviour and where its inputs, training data, and outputs live
options.B: That any regression qualifies as AI
options.C: That the claim exempts the product from testing
options.D: That linear models need no validation

questions.explanation: Scoping starts by locating the learning components and their data flows rather than accepting the label at face value.

questions.question: Why is the training-serving skew problem relevant already at project scoping time?

options.A: If serving data will differ from training data, the test strategy must cover that gap from the start
options.C: Training and serving data are always identical

questions.explanation: Anticipated differences between training and live data shape requirements for test data, monitoring, and acceptance criteria.

questions.question: A team must choose between supervised classification and clustering for a fraud-detection task with few labelled cases. What is the correct reasoning?

options.A: Supervised learning needs sufficient labels, so with few labels the team should consider semi-supervised or unsupervised approaches plus a labelling plan
options.C: Labels are irrelevant to the choice
options.D: Supervised learning works without any labels

questions.explanation: The availability of labelled data is the decisive factor, and the strategy must address the labelling gap explicitly.

questions.question: Why does the choice of loss function matter to the tester?

options.A: It defines what the model optimises, so test oracles and metrics must align with the same objective
options.B: Loss functions only affect training speed
options.C: Testers never need to know the loss
options.D: All loss functions produce identical models

questions.explanation: A model optimised for one objective may fail a differently defined acceptance test, so the test basis must match the optimisation goal.

questions.question: What does the bias-variance trade-off imply for test planning?

options.A: Both underfitting and overfitting must be checked, requiring separate training, validation, and held-out test assessments

questions.explanation: Tests must distinguish a model too simple to capture patterns from one memorising noise, which demands disciplined data splits.

questions.question: A model achieves 99 percent training accuracy but 70 percent on held-out data. What does this gap indicate?

options.A: Overfitting: the model memorised training specifics that do not generalise
options.C: A labelling error in the test set only

questions.explanation: A large train-test gap is the signature of overfitting, directing remediation toward regularisation, more data, or simpler hypotheses.

questions.question: Why should the tester insist on a locked test set that the training team never sees?

options.A: Exposure lets modelling choices overfit to the test set, invalidating it as an unbiased estimate
options.C: Test data should always be shared
options.D: Locking is only for regulated projects

questions.explanation: Any feedback from test results into modelling leaks information and inflates the estimate, so the final set must stay sealed.

questions.question: What is the testing implication of non-deterministic training?

options.A: Repeated training runs may yield different models, so acceptance must tolerate variance and verify stability across runs
options.D: A single run is always sufficient

questions.explanation: Stochastic optimisation means the delivered model is one sample among many, and tests must confirm the process is stable, not just one artefact.

questions.question: Why must data preprocessing steps be tested independently of the model?

options.A: A defect in scaling, encoding, or imputation corrupts every downstream result regardless of model quality

questions.explanation: The pipeline is only as sound as its first stages, so transformations must be verified with their own oracles before model testing.

questions.question: A pipeline joins three data sources on a customer identifier. What defect should the tester specifically probe?

options.A: Join mismatches such as duplicates, missing keys, and type inconsistencies that silently change the training distribution
options.D: The office location of the data team

questions.explanation: Join defects alter which rows train the model and can leak future information, so key integrity and row-count reconciliation are essential.

questions.question: What is the purpose of testing the feature store separately from model training?

options.A: To confirm that training and serving consume identical feature definitions and values
options.C: Training features are always identical to serving features
options.D: Feature stores only affect storage cost

questions.explanation: Skew between offline and online features is a leading cause of production failure, so parity must be verified explicitly.

questions.question: How should a tester verify a data labelling process?

options.A: By measuring inter-annotator agreement on samples and adjudicating disagreements with documented guidelines
options.B: By trusting the first label produced
options.D: By skipping guidelines to save time

questions.explanation: Agreement metrics plus guideline-driven adjudication quantify and control the noise that labels inject into training.

questions.question: Why test the model export and packaging step even when training metrics look good?

options.A: Serialisation, quantisation, or graph conversion can change numerical behaviour between training and deployment

questions.explanation: The artefact that serves is the converted model, so parity between the evaluated model and the deployed artefact must be confirmed.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: A training set contains duplicate records spanning the train-test split. What is the consequence?

options.A: Leakage inflates test scores because the model is evaluated on data it has already seen
options.D: Splits are irrelevant with enough data

questions.explanation: Cross-split duplicates let memorisation masquerade as generalisation, so deduplication across splits is mandatory.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: How should a tester check for selection bias in training data?

options.A: By comparing the demographic and feature distributions against the target population the system will serve
options.B: By counting the total number of rows

questions.explanation: Under-represented groups or conditions produce models that fail those segments, so distribution comparison against the target is the check.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: What does a sudden shift in input feature distributions after deployment signal?

options.A: Data drift that may invalidate the model's assumptions and warrants investigation and possible retraining

questions.explanation: Drift monitoring on inputs is the early warning that the world has moved away from the training distribution.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: Why test for label leakage in the feature set?

options.A: Features that encode the answer let the model cheat during training and collapse in production

questions.explanation: Leaky features produce spectacular offline scores and catastrophic live failures, so temporal and causal audits of features are required.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: A categorical feature has 5 percent missing values. What should the tester verify?

options.A: That the imputation strategy is documented, consistent between training and serving, and its impact is measured
options.B: That missing values are ignored silently
options.C: That the rows are deleted without record

questions.explanation: Inconsistent or undocumented imputation creates serving skew, so the strategy and its effect must be explicit and tested.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: How can adversarial examples in the input test set improve robustness assessment?

options.A: They probe the model's behaviour on worst-case perturbed inputs that natural test data may never contain
options.B: Adversarial examples are only for security audits
options.C: They always degrade measured accuracy unfairly
options.D: They replace the need for natural test data

questions.explanation: Crafted perturbations reveal brittle decision boundaries that identically distributed test sets cannot expose.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: What is the testing value of a data schema with explicit constraints?

options.A: It provides executable oracles for validating every batch before it enters training or serving

questions.explanation: Enforced schemas catch type, range, and completeness violations early, preventing corrupt data from silently degrading the model.

questions.question: Accuracy is 95 percent but the minority class recall is 40 percent. What should the tester conclude?

options.A: The headline metric hides a critical failure on the class that likely matters most
options.B: The model is ready for release
options.C: Recall is irrelevant when accuracy is high
options.D: The minority class needs no coverage

questions.explanation: Aggregate accuracy masks per-class performance, so class-level metrics aligned with business cost must drive the verdict.

questions.question: Why use a confusion matrix rather than a single accuracy figure for acceptance?

options.A: It reveals which error types dominate so the business cost of each can be weighed

questions.explanation: Different confusions carry different costs, and only the matrix shows whether the errors are the affordable kind.

questions.question: What does a precision-recall curve communicate that a single F1 score does not?

options.A: The trade-off across all thresholds, letting stakeholders choose the operating point that matches their cost ratio

questions.explanation: A single score fixes one threshold implicitly, while the curve exposes the full frontier for an informed choice.

questions.question: How should a tester validate a model that outputs calibrated probabilities?

options.A: By checking reliability diagrams or calibration error so stated confidences match observed frequencies

questions.explanation: Downstream decisions depend on the probabilities meaning what they claim, so calibration must be measured explicitly.

questions.question: A model passes offline tests but its online A/B test shows no lift. What is the most likely explanation?

options.A: Offline metrics did not capture the true business objective or the online context differs from the test setup
options.D: A/B tests cannot measure ML impact

questions.explanation: Misalignment between offline proxies and online goals, or context differences, explains the gap and must be investigated.

questions.question: Why test model behaviour on out-of-distribution inputs explicitly?

options.A: Production inevitably presents unfamiliar inputs, and the model's failure mode there must be known and bounded
options.D: It only matters for research models

questions.explanation: Characterising degradation outside the training envelope lets the team set guardrails instead of discovering failures live.

questions.question: What is metamorphic testing's value when no exact oracle exists?

options.A: Relations between inputs and expected output changes provide checkable properties without knowing the exact answer
options.C: It only works for sorting algorithms

questions.explanation: Properties such as monotonicity or invariance give verifiable assertions where ground truth is unavailable.

questions.question: How should fairness be tested for a credit-scoring model?

options.A: By comparing approval rates and error rates across protected groups with predefined tolerance bands
options.D: By testing on a single group

questions.explanation: Disaggregated metrics reveal disparate impact that aggregate scores conceal, and tolerance bands make the verdict objective.

questions.question: What does testing for robustness to input noise establish?

options.A: Whether small realistic perturbations cause disproportionate output changes that would break user trust
options.C: That models are immune to noise

questions.explanation: Real inputs contain typos, blur, and sensor noise, so stability under such perturbations is a release criterion.

questions.question: Why compare a complex model against a simple baseline during testing?

options.A: To confirm the added complexity earns its keep in measurable improvement

questions.explanation: A baseline sets the bar the sophisticated model must clear to justify its cost and opacity.

questions.question: Why is end-to-end testing of an AI-based system different from testing the model alone?

options.A: System behaviour emerges from the model plus surrounding software, data pipelines, and human workflows
options.C: Systems need no testing beyond the model

questions.explanation: Integration effects, feedback loops, and human interaction create failures no component test can reveal.

questions.question: A recommendation system degrades as users adapt their behaviour to its outputs. What is this phenomenon?

options.A: A feedback loop where the system's outputs reshape its future inputs, requiring longitudinal testing

questions.explanation: Self-reinforcing loops change the data distribution over time, so testing must track behaviour across retraining cycles.

questions.question: How should a tester approach a system whose requirements are expressed as statistical targets?

options.A: Design tests that estimate the target with confidence intervals over sufficient samples
options.B: Test a single case and extrapolate

questions.explanation: Probabilistic requirements demand sampling methodology, not single-case verdicts, with sample sizes matched to the claimed precision.

questions.question: What is the role of a human oracle in testing generative outputs?

options.A: To judge qualities such as coherence and appropriateness that automated metrics approximate poorly

questions.explanation: For open-ended generation, human assessment remains the reference that automated proxies must be calibrated against.

questions.question: Why must test environments for AI systems control for randomness explicitly?

options.A: Uncontrolled seeds and nondeterministic execution make failures unreproducible and results incomparable

questions.explanation: Fixing seeds and isolating stochastic components is what makes a test result attributable rather than accidental.

questions.question: A vision system fails only at dusk. What testing lesson does this illustrate?

options.A: Operational conditions such as lighting must be part of the test basis, not just the object classes

questions.explanation: Environmental coverage is as important as content coverage for perception systems.

questions.question: Why is autonomy a distinct quality concern for AI-based systems?

options.A: Autonomous decisions act without human review, so the cost of an error and the need for safeguards scale with independence

questions.explanation: The less human oversight intervenes, the more the system itself must be verified to behave safely.

questions.question: How does opacity complicate defect diagnosis in ML systems?

options.A: Failures cannot be traced to an explicit rule, so diagnosis relies on data analysis and experimentation

questions.explanation: Without inspectable logic, testers must infer causes from input-output behaviour and targeted probes.

questions.question: What does adaptability imply for regression testing of learning systems?

options.A: Retrained models must be re-verified because behaviour can change even when code is untouched
options.D: Code changes are the only risk

questions.explanation: Each retraining produces a new behavioural artefact, so the regression suite must run against every released model, not just code changes.

questions.question: Why is data quality a quality characteristic of the system rather than just an input concern?

options.A: The model's behaviour is a function of its data, so data defects are system defects
options.D: Data is external to the system

questions.explanation: In learned systems the data is effectively part of the implementation, elevating its quality to a first-class concern.

questions.question: A chatbot's answers vary subtly between identical queries. Which characteristic does this challenge?

options.A: Repeatability and consistency, which must be bounded before outputs can be trusted in regulated use

questions.explanation: Non-determinism must be characterised and constrained where decisions depend on stable answers.

questions.question: Why does explainability matter more for a loan-approval model than for a movie recommender?

options.A: Regulatory and ethical obligations require justifying consequential decisions to affected individuals

questions.explanation: The stakes of the decision determine how much transparency the system must provide.

questions.question: How should robustness be specified as a testable requirement?

options.A: As the maximum acceptable performance degradation under defined perturbations such as noise levels or missing fields
options.B: As a vague statement that the system should be robust
options.D: As a requirement on training speed

questions.explanation: Quantified perturbation bounds turn robustness from an aspiration into a verifiable acceptance criterion.

questions.question: What makes maintainability harder for ML systems than for conventional software?

options.A: Behaviour depends on data, pipelines, and model artefacts in addition to code, multiplying what must be versioned and tracked

questions.explanation: The expanded surface of code plus data plus models demands broader configuration management and lineage tracking.

questions.question: Why is monitorability itself a quality characteristic for deployed AI?

options.A: Silent degradation is the default failure mode, so the system must expose signals that reveal it

questions.explanation: Without designed-in telemetry for inputs, outputs, and decisions, drift and decay go unnoticed until users complain.

questions.question: A test harness compares model outputs against human labels but disagrees on ambiguous cases. How should this be resolved?

options.A: Define adjudication rules and measure harness-label agreement before trusting automated verdicts

questions.explanation: The test infrastructure itself must be validated where ground truth is subjective, or verdicts reflect harness bias.

questions.question: A product team wants to add an AI feature with no measurable success criterion. What should the tester recommend?

options.A: Define a quantitative evaluation with a baseline before development, so progress and readiness can be judged

questions.explanation: Unmeasurable objectives cannot be tested, so establishing metrics and baselines is a precondition for the work.

questions.question: Two models have equal accuracy but very different calibration. Which should be preferred for a risk-scoring use case?

options.A: The better-calibrated one, because decisions depend on the probabilities being meaningful

questions.explanation: When thresholds drive actions, trustworthy probabilities outweigh headline accuracy.

questions.question: A feature pipeline caches transformed features for speed. What risk must be tested?

options.A: Stale cache entries serving outdated values to training or inference after upstream data changes

questions.explanation: Invalidation correctness is critical because silent staleness corrupts both model training and live decisions.

questions.domain: Input Data Testing for ML Systems
questions.question: Time-series data is split randomly instead of chronologically. What defect does this introduce?

options.A: Future information leaks into training, producing optimistic estimates that collapse on genuinely future data
options.C: Chronology is irrelevant for time series

questions.explanation: Temporal ordering must be respected in splits, otherwise the model learns from the future it must predict.

questions.question: A regression model shows low mean error but large errors on high-value transactions. What should change?

options.A: The evaluation must weight errors by business impact rather than treating all rows equally

questions.explanation: Unweighted averages hide costly tail errors, so impact-weighted metrics must drive acceptance.

questions.question: An AI feature is updated weekly with retrained models. What release practice is essential?

options.A: Automated regression of each candidate model plus staged rollout with production quality monitoring

questions.explanation: Frequent model refreshes demand a repeatable verification pipeline and guarded rollout, not ad-hoc releases.

questions.question: An insurance model is retrained monthly on new claims. What must the release checklist include?

options.A: Verification that the new model meets all quality gates on a fixed benchmark suite before replacing the old one
options.B: Replacing the model automatically without checks

questions.explanation: Scheduled retraining still requires gate checks on every candidate, since new data can degrade previously passing behaviour.
